subject: physics
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: The velocity in SHM as a function of displacement x is v = ±ω√(A²−x²). At equilibrium (x=0), the speed is:
questions.explain: At x = 0 the speed is maximum, equal to ωA.

questions.q: Specific latent heat is the energy needed to change the state of:
options: 1 kg of substance at constant temperature
questions.explain: Specific latent heat is the energy per kilogram to change state at constant temperature.

questions.q: According to the Rayleigh criterion, two point sources are just resolved by a telescope of aperture D at wavelength λ when their angular separation is approximately:
questions.explain: The Rayleigh criterion for a circular aperture gives the minimum resolvable angle θ ≈ 1.22 λ/D.

questions.q: For a mass m on a spring of stiffness k, the period of SHM is:
questions.explain: The period of a mass–spring oscillator is T = 2π√(m/k).

questions.q: For an ideal gas, the internal energy depends only on:
questions.explain: An ideal gas has no intermolecular potential energy, so internal energy depends only on temperature.

questions.q: In SHM, the maximum acceleration of an oscillator of amplitude A is:
questions.explain: Maximum acceleration a_max = ω²A, occurring at maximum displacement.

questions.q: When two objects are in thermal equilibrium, they have the same:
questions.explain: Thermal equilibrium means no net heat flow, which occurs when temperatures are equal.

questions.q: During a change of state (e.g. melting), the temperature of the substance:
questions.explain: During a change of state temperature stays constant as energy alters particle potential energy.

questions.q: During SHM, total mechanical energy (in the absence of damping):
options: Stays constant as KE and PE interchange
questions.explain: Total energy is constant; kinetic and potential energy interchange throughout the cycle.

questions.q: The absolute magnitude of a star is defined as the apparent magnitude it would have if placed at a distance of:
questions.explain: Absolute magnitude M is the apparent magnitude a star would have at a standard distance of 10 parsecs.

questions.q: Stefan's law for the luminosity (power output) of a star of surface area A and temperature T is:
questions.explain: Stefan's law gives L = σ A T⁴, so luminosity rises with the fourth power of absolute temperature.

questions.q: At the equilibrium position in SHM, the energy is:
questions.explain: At equilibrium displacement is zero so PE is minimum and KE is maximum.

questions.q: A free oscillation occurs when a system oscillates at its:
options: Natural frequency with no external periodic force
questions.explain: Free oscillations occur at the natural frequency with no external driving force.

questions.q: The specific heat capacity equation is:
questions.explain: Energy to change temperature is Q = mcΔT.

questions.q: In the transit method of exoplanet detection, a planet is inferred from:
options: the planet's own emitted radio waves
a permanent red shift of the star
a periodic small dip in the star's brightness as the planet passes in front
a steady increase in the star's temperature
questions.explain: As an exoplanet crosses in front of its star, it blocks a little light, causing a regular dip in the measured brightness.

questions.q: A real gas behaves most like an ideal gas at:
questions.explain: At low pressure and high temperature molecules are far apart with negligible interactions.

questions.q: The root-mean-square (rms) speed of gas molecules is found by:
options: Taking the square root of the mean of the squared speeds
questions.explain: The rms speed is √⟨c²⟩, the square root of the mean of the squared speeds.

questions.q: Charles's law states that at constant pressure, the volume of a fixed mass of gas is proportional to:
questions.explain: At constant pressure V ∝ T (absolute temperature in kelvin).

questions.q: Which sequence correctly describes the evolution of a low-mass star like the Sun?
options: red giant → main sequence → nebula → white dwarf
nebula → red giant → main sequence → supernova
main sequence → neutron star → black hole
nebula → main sequence → red giant → white dwarf
questions.explain: A Sun-like star forms from a nebula, fuses on the main sequence, swells into a red giant, then sheds its layers leaving a white dwarf.

questions.q: The mean kinetic energy of a molecule in an ideal gas is given by:
questions.explain: Mean translational kinetic energy per molecule is (3/2)kT.

questions.q: In the standard OBAFGKM spectral classification, which sequence is ordered from hottest to coolest?
options: G, F, A, B, O, K, M
M, K, G, F, A, B, O
A, B, O, F, G, K, M
O, B, A, F, G, K, M
questions.explain: The spectral sequence O B A F G K M runs from the hottest (O) to the coolest (M) stars.

questions.q: Dark energy is the term used to explain which observation about the universe?
options: that all stars have the same mass
that light bends around the Sun
that the expansion of the universe is accelerating
questions.explain: Observations of distant Type Ia supernovae show the cosmic expansion is accelerating, attributed to dark energy.

questions.q: The cosmic microwave background radiation is strong evidence for the Big Bang because it is:
options: an almost uniform microwave glow from all directions with a black-body spectrum near 2.7 K
coming from a single nearby galaxy
the light of the nearest stars red-shifted slightly
questions.explain: The CMB is nearly isotropic radiation with a 2.7 K black-body spectrum, the cooled remnant of a hot early universe.

questions.q: After a massive star explodes as a supernova, the dense remnant left behind is a neutron star or, if massive enough:
questions.explain: If the collapsing core exceeds the neutron-star mass limit, gravity overwhelms all support and a black hole forms.

questions.q: For circular motion, which expression for centripetal acceleration uses angular speed ω?
questions.explain: Since v = ωr, the acceleration v²/r equals ω²r.

questions.q: For a refracting telescope in normal adjustment, the angular magnification is given by which expression?
questions.explain: Angular magnification M = fo/fe, the ratio of the objective focal length to the eyepiece focal length.

questions.q: Hubble's law relates the recession velocity v of a galaxy to its distance d by:
questions.explain: Hubble's law is v = H₀ d, with the recession velocity proportional to distance.

questions.q: Increasing the diameter of a telescope's objective improves its ability to see faint objects mainly because the collecting power is proportional to:
options: the square root of the aperture
questions.explain: Collecting power scales with the area of the aperture, which is proportional to diameter squared.

questions.q: Dark matter was first inferred largely because:
options: stars in galaxies rotate faster than the visible mass alone can explain
galaxies emit too much visible light
questions.explain: Galaxy rotation curves stay flat at large radii, implying far more (non-luminous) mass than we can see.

questions.q: The kinetic theory equation is pV = ⅓Nm⟨c²⟩, where ⟨c²⟩ is the:
questions.explain: ⟨c²⟩ is the mean square speed of the molecules.
